# Tabsdata documentation

> Documentation for Tabsdata 2.3.0, an AI-first data integration (ETL/ELT) platform built for agentic data engineering: an AI agent carries a data request end to end inside one system, from discovery through build to regression test, and a human approves every change. Python functions publish data from sources into versioned tables, transform them and subscribe them to destinations. Orchestration, execution, monitoring, lineage, data quality and versioning are native to the same server and the same `tdk` CLI, with one data model and one set of ids, so an agent works from one vocabulary. Two views of the guide: the Agentic guide at /guide gives steps an agent can follow; the Developer guide at /developer/guide gives concepts, configuration and reference for engineers working by hand.

Local quick start: Python 3.12, `pip install "tabsdata[all]"`, `tdkserver quickstart -y --details false`, then `tdk login --server localhost --user admin --password tabsdata`. The UI is at http://localhost:2457, the API on the same port. The default instance is named `tabsdata`. The `tabsdata` package on PyPI is Tabsdata Enterprise, built on the Apache-licensed open source Tabsdata on GitHub; the full platform is free for self-supported deployments, with no feature gates.

Vocabulary: a project holds collections; a collection holds functions and the tables they produce, and a source or destination collection carries the connection (address and credentials) its functions share. A publisher reads an external system into tables, a transformer reads tables and writes tables, a subscriber writes tables to an external system, a stream publisher consumes Kafka or CDC continuously. Triggering a function builds an execution plan over every downstream function; it runs as transactions, function runs and workers, and table versions commit only when the whole plan succeeds.

Every page is also available as markdown: append `.md` to its URL, as in https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/lineage.md. [llms-full.txt](https://docs.tabsdata.com/llms-full.txt) holds every page listed below in one file.

## Tasks

- [Load CSV or Parquet files from S3 into Snowflake every night](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/amazon-s3): a publisher from S3, a subscriber to Snowflake, a cron trigger.
- [Replicate a Postgres, MySQL or Db2 database to a warehouse with change data capture](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/postgres-cdc): consistent full load, then change capture.
- [Pull Salesforce reports or SOQL queries into a database](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/salesforce-reports): `SalesforceReportSrc`, a report found by name or id, incremental reads on a last-modified column.
- [Stream Kafka topics into tables](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/kafka): a stream publisher with `KafkaStreamSrc`, a schema, and a dead-letter topic for messages that fail to decode.
- [Join, dedupe and clean tables from two systems before loading them](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/join-tables): Python over a TableFrame.
- [Run a transformation whenever an upstream table gets new data](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/trigger-setup/table-commit): `trigger_by` picks which input tables start the function; an empty list turns automatic runs off.
- [Deliver tables to BigQuery, Databricks, ClickHouse, Postgres, S3 or a catalog](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/): one subscriber per destination, Unity Catalog included.
- [Find out why last night's load failed or produced no data](https://docs.tabsdata.com/cli/tdk): `tdk plan get`, `tdk plan logs`, `tdk worker logs`, execution plans.
- [See what changed in a table since the last run, and where a row came from](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/lineage): every run is a new version; lineage comes from execution.
- [Track data quality over time](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/data-quality-trends): metrics kept by run, week and month.


## For AI agents

- [Configure Your AI Agent](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connect-agent): install the Tabsdata skill for your coding agent with `tdk ai agents install`, then log in with `tdk login` from your own terminal so the agent acts through your session.
- [tdk CLI reference](https://docs.tabsdata.com/cli/tdk): every command: projects, groups, collections, connections, functions and their runs, plans, transactions, workers, tables, streams, crons, permissions, users, metrics, examples; `tdk login`, `tdk settings`, `tdk shell`.
- [Python API reference](https://docs.tabsdata.com/api/): decorators, TableFrame, connector classes and credentials, with an alphabetical index.

## Guide

- [Contact Support](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/operations/contact-support): Lists the Tabsdata contact channels: the company website, the community Slack workspace invite, and the GitHub repository.

## Getting Started

- [Introduction](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/introduction): Tabsdata overview covering Python functions as workflows, Polars expression transforms, automatic DAG orchestration, data versioning, the tdk coding agent skill, and built-in connectors for Snowflake, S3, Postgres, MySQL, and Databricks.
- [Install Tabsdata](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/install): Installs the Tabsdata Python package with pip or uv, creates a virtual environment, sets the Anthropic or OpenAI LLM key, runs tdkserver quickstart with the kminus provider, and logs in.
- [Configure Your AI Agent](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connect-agent): Install the Tabsdata skill so a coding agent works with Tabsdata through tdk in its own shell, then log in so the agent acts through your session.
- [Run Your First Data Integration](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/run-your-first-data-integration): Quickstart that has a coding agent build a Tabsdata workflow from a CSV: publisher, transformer adding full_name and dropping age, and subscriber writing people.jsonl, then checking the UI.

## Architecture

- [Architecture Overview](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/architecture): Tabsdata system architecture: resource layer (Functions, Tables) and execution layer (Execution Plans, Transactions, Function Runs), plus scalability, security, deployment providers, and AI integration.
- [Server](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/server): What a Tabsdata server contains, how it runs workflows, and how clients connect to it.
- [Projects](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/projects): How Projects organize and isolate resources within a Tabsdata Server.
- [Groups](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/groups): How Groups organize Collections by data direction and transformation stage.
- [Collections](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/collections): How Collections contain Functions, Tables, and Connections and define transaction boundaries.
- [Connections](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connections): How Connections provide Publisher and Subscriber Functions with access to external systems.
- [Functions](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/functions/): How Tabsdata Functions define, connect, and execute the steps in a data workflow.
- [Publishers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/functions/publishers): How @publisher reads an external system, maps source slots to function parameters, and writes versioned Tabsdata tables.
- [Stream Publishers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/functions/stream-publishers): How @stream_publisher reads a CDC log or a Kafka topic continuously, and how the batch parameters decide when the function runs.
- [Transformers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/functions/transformers): How @transformer reads Tabsdata tables, maps versions to function parameters, and commits transformed output tables.
- [Subscribers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/functions/subscribers): How @subscriber reads Tabsdata tables, maps function returns to destination slots, and writes to an external system.
- [Tables](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/tables): Covers Tabsdata Tables as persistent, versioned stores of function output: version history, the table reference format (`collection/table@version` with HEAD, INITIAL, and ranges), private `_` tables, and commit-based triggers.
- [Execution Plans](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/execution/execution-plans): Explains the execution plan DAG Tabsdata builds when a Function is triggered, how Functions pass data through Tables, determinism, and the tdk plan, trx, fnrun, and worker commands.
- [Transactions](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/execution/transactions): Explains how transactions group Table changes within a Collection so they commit together, preserve pristine state on failure, and make execution plans multi-transactional across Collections.
- [Function Runs](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/execution/function-runs): Function Runs cover how each Function execution in an Execution Plan is tracked, including status, logs, Worker assignment, recovery, and replay, with CLI commands linked.
- [Workers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/execution/workers): Explains what a Tabsdata worker is, how retries work (three attempts by default), and the tdk worker logs, recover, and list commands with their filters.

## Connectors

- [Connectors](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/): The connectors built into Tabsdata, and the source and destination classes each one provides.
- [Connector Overview](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/): The connectors built into Tabsdata, and the source and destination classes each one provides.
- [Schema Evolution](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/schema-evolution): What strict and update do when a write brings a new column or a wider type, per table destination: the write behavior matrix, type widening, native and Iceberg schema evolution, and the permissions update needs.
- [Object Store Options](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/object-store-options): The obstore.* keys that configure the object store behind the file connectors and the staging locations: which keys each provider takes, where they are set, and what they override.
- [SQL Merge](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/functions/sql-merge): How Subscriber Functions apply inserts, updates, and deletes to Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks tables.
- [Amazon S3](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/amazon-s3): Reference for the Tabsdata Amazon S3 connector.
- [Apache Druid](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/druid): Reference for the Tabsdata Apache Druid destination connector, cloud staging, and subscriber configuration.
- [Azure](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/azure): Reference for the Tabsdata Azure Blob Storage connector.
- [BigQuery](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/bigquery): Reference for the Tabsdata BigQuery connector.
- [ClickHouse](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/clickhouse): Reference for the Tabsdata ClickHouse destination connector, cloud staging, and subscriber configuration.
- [Databricks](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/databricks): Reference for the Tabsdata Databricks connector.
- [Db2](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/db2): Reference for the Tabsdata Db2 connector.
- [Db2 CDC](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/db2-cdc): Reference for the Tabsdata Db2 CDC stream source: SQL Replication prerequisites, the full load, change rows, and the connection.
- [Google Cloud Storage](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/gcp): Reference for the Tabsdata Google Cloud Storage connector.
- [Kafka](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/kafka): Reference for the Tabsdata Kafka stream source: message formats, schema registries, dead letter topics, consumer groups, and the connection.
- [Local File System](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/local-file-system): Reference for the Tabsdata Local File System connector.
- [MariaDB](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/mariadb): Reference for the Tabsdata MariaDB connector.
- [MongoDB](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/mongodb): Reference for the Tabsdata MongoDB destination connector and subscriber configuration.
- [MSSQL](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/mssql): Reference for the Tabsdata MSSQL connector.
- [MySQL](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/mysql): Reference for the Tabsdata MySQL connector.
- [MySQL CDC](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/mysql-cdc): Reference for the Tabsdata MySQL CDC stream source: prerequisites, the full load, change rows, and the connection.
- [Oracle](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/oracle): Reference for the Tabsdata Oracle connector.
- [Postgres](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/postgres): Reference for the Tabsdata Postgres connector.
- [Postgres CDC](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/postgres-cdc): Reference for the Tabsdata Postgres CDC stream source: prerequisites, the full load, change rows, and the connection.
- [Salesforce](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/salesforce): Reference for the Tabsdata Salesforce connectors: SOQL queries, reports, and the shared connection.
- [Snowflake](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/snowflake): Reference for the Tabsdata Snowflake connector.
- [StarRocks](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/connectors/starrocks): Reference for the Tabsdata StarRocks destination connector, cloud staging, and subscriber configuration.
- [Grok for Log Files](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/grok-for-log-files): Grok method of TableFrame parses string columns into typed columns using Grok patterns and a ColumnDefinition schema, with predefined patterns, repeated captures, and null handling for non-matching rows.
- [Custom Connectors](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/plugins): Guide to building a custom Tabsdata connector as a Python package: SQLite source and destination, entry points, error codes, installation, and use in Functions.

## Orchestration and Triggers

- [Automatic Orchestration](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/automatic-orchestration): How Tabsdata determines which functions to run and in what order based on the tables they read and write.
- [Trigger Overview](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/execution-and-triggers): Covers the four Tabsdata function trigger types (manual via `tdk fn trigger` or the UI, CRON schedule, new-data on input table versions, and stream workers such as SQL CDC and Kafka), plus automatic execution plans and streaming publishers.
- [Manual Triggers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/triggers/manual): Covers triggering a Tabsdata Function by hand with `tdk fn trigger` from the CLI or the UI, the default for Publishers without `trigger_by`, and how the resulting Execution Plan runs downstream Functions.
- [Cron Triggers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/triggers/cron): Cron triggers in Tabsdata: crontab mask syntax with UTC schedules, optional start and end window, and enabling or disabling Functions with tdk fn enable and disable. Wait, that's over-long and has a colon-style fragment. Corrected: Cron Triggers: five-field Unix crontab masks run in UTC, optional start and end windows, and enabling or disabling Functions with tdk fn enable/disable.
- [Table Commit Triggers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/triggers/table-commit): Configures Table commit triggers via the `trigger_by` decorator option: default, empty-list, and named-Table behavior, cross-Collection `collection/table` references, and returning None to skip commits.
- [Stream Triggers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/triggers/stream): Stream trigger page: when a @stream_publisher batch is due (batch_min_secs, batch_max_secs, batch_max_rows, batch_max_bytes, batch_idle_secs) and the Kafka, MySQL CDC, Postgres CDC, and Db2 CDC stream sources.

## Features

- [Secrets Management](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/secrets-management/): Explains how to register credentials in Tabsdata Connections via `tdk connection template` and `tdk collection create`/`update`, the dehydration into a secret store, `$secret:<VARIABLE>` environment references, and the security tradeoffs of passing secrets to a coding agent.
- [Service Tokens](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/service-tokens): How a service token lets CI jobs, schedulers and scripts call Tabsdata as its owner without a password, and which of the owner's permissions it carries.
- [User Interface](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/user-interface): Tabsdata web UI pages for the Overview, Projects, Collections, Functions, Tables, Executions, Worker logs, Triggers, Search, Tabby, Security, System, and Account, plus the local URL and demo.
- [Tabby](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/tabby): The built-in operational agent, opened from the UI. It answers questions about the server's resources, monitors dataflows, traces failures to root cause and suggests fixes, and, when the server allows it, creates and changes resources on request. It runs in the server's AI agent service (port 2459) and needs an Anthropic or OpenAI key, set with `tdkserver quickstart --config anthropic-key=env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- [Data Quality](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/data-quality): Data quality checks in Tabsdata: DataQuality classifiers (IsNotNull, IsBetween, IsIn, Matches, ScaleCategorizer) and operators (Filter, Select, Summary, Fail, Enrich) passed via on_tables to publishers and transformers.
- [Data Quality Trends](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/data-quality-trends): How Summary(trends=Trends()) keeps a history of data quality checks in a trend Table, and how the Tabsdata UI charts it.
- [Lineage](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/lineage): How Tabsdata records where each table version came from and how to view that lineage in the Tabsdata UI.
- [Living Semantic Catalog](https://docs.tabsdata.com/guide/living-semantic-catalog): How Tabsdata builds a catalog of what every connected source and destination holds, keeps it current as those systems change, and how agents use it.

## Tutorials: Publish data from

- [Amazon S3](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/amazon-s3): Publish data from Amazon S3 into Tabsdata with S3Src publishers, covering bucket connection setup, glob paths like trips_*.parquet, multiple files, and the format option.
- [Azure Blob Storage](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/azure): Publishes CSV and other blobs from an Azure Blob Storage container into Tabsdata tables, covering `AzureBlobSrc` paths and globs, the `AzureBlobSrcConn` connection, account key credentials, `file_info`, and `initial_last_modified`.
- [Databricks](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/databricks): Publishes Databricks SQL query results into Tabsdata tables via the DatabricksSrc connector, covering `queries`, `initial_values` placeholders, warehouse and staging volume settings.
- [Db2](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/db2): Publishes query results from a Db2 database into Tabsdata via the db2+ibm_db connector, with Db2Src queries, output tables, and connection setup.
- [Db2 CDC](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/db2-cdc): Covers publishing Db2 change data capture with @stream_publisher and Db2CdcStreamSrc: tables, start_from options (tail, full, head), batch_max_secs, and output_tables.
- [Google Cloud Storage](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/gcp): Publishes objects from a Google Cloud Storage bucket into Tabsdata tables, covering GCSSrc paths, service account JSON credentials, base_path, and initial_last_modified.
- [Grok for Log Files](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/grok-for-log-files): Parses single-column log files into typed TableFrame columns with the grok function, using Elasticsearch-style patterns, named captures, and a schema, from LocalFileSrc or object storage publishers.
- [Kafka](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/kafka): Publishes a Kafka topic into a Tabsdata table with the @stream_publisher decorator and KafkaStreamSrc, covering schema, dlq_topic, and batch_max_secs/batch_max_bytes settings.
- [Local Files](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/local-file-system): Shows how to publish a local CSV file as a Tabsdata table by defining a LocalFileSrcConn connection with base_path, a publisher with LocalFileSrc source, and output_tables, and verifying the result.
- [MariaDB](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/mariadb): Publishes MariaDB tables to Tabsdata with the MySQL connector: MySQLSrcConn and MySQLSrc setup and per-query output tables.
- [MSSQL](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/mssql): Publishes SQL Server query results to Tabsdata with an MSSQLSrc source, covering the mssql+pyodbc connection URI, ODBC driver setting, credentials, and the queries and output_tables options.
- [MySQL](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/mysql): Publishes query results from a MySQL database into Tabsdata tables using MySQLSrc, a connectionDef YAML, and secret references.
- [MySQL CDC](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/mysql-cdc): Publishes MySQL binlog changes to Tabsdata tables with @stream_publisher and MySQLCdcStreamSrc, covering start_from options and batch_max_secs.
- [Oracle](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/oracle): Publishes query results from an Oracle database into Tabsdata with the OracleSrc source, covering the oracledb driver requirement, connection YAML, and the queries and output_tables arguments of @publisher.
- [Postgres](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/postgres): Publishes Postgres query results into Tabsdata tables using the PostgresSrc source, a connectionDef YAML with user and password credentials, and the psycopg2-binary driver requirement.
- [Postgres CDC](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/postgres-cdc): Publishes Postgres CDC changes from tracked tables via @stream_publisher and a logical replication slot, covering PostgresCdcStreamSrc options, start_from, and slot behavior.
- [Salesforce Reports](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/salesforce-reports): Publishes Salesforce report data into Tabsdata using SalesforceReportSrc, covering report name or id lookup with find_report_by, column_name_strategy, filter and filter_logic options, and incremental last_modified_column.
- [Salesforce SOQL Query](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/publishers/salesforce): Publishes Salesforce SOQL query results into Tabsdata tables with incremental reads via SystemModStamp and $lastModified, initial_last_modified, and include_deleted options.

## Tutorials: Transform data

- [Create a TableFrame](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/create-a-tableframe): Shows how to create a TableFrame programmatically from a Python dict, Pandas DataFrame, or Polars LazyFrame/DataFrame via `from_dict`, `from_pandas`, and `from_polars`, and how to convert back with `to_dict`, `to_pandas`, `to_polars_df`, and `to_polars_lf`.
- [Select and Modify Columns](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/select-columns): Projection in Tabsdata transformers: select(), drop(), with_columns(), rename(), and the cs selectors (cs.numeric, cs.starts_with, cs.by_index, cs.exclude, lit).
- [Filter Rows](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/filter-rows): Filter rows in a Tabsdata transformer with filter() using col() comparisons, &, |, ~, xor, is_in, is_between, is_null, is_not_nan, and unique() with subset and keep.
- [Transform Strings](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/strings): Covers Tabsdata string transformations via the str accessor: changing case, matching and extracting with contains, starts_with, ends_with and regex, replacing, trimming, padding, slicing, measuring lengths and finding positions, and parsing log lines with grok.
- [Transform Numbers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/numbers): Arithmetic, rounding, powers, logs, trigonometry, and row-to-row differences for Tabsdata table columns, with the transformer code for each operator and method.
- [Transform Dates and Times](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/dates-and-times): Extracts date and time components, shifts dates, truncates timestamps, converts durations to totals, handles time zones, and formats dates with dt accessors in Tabsdata.
- [Aggregate and Group](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/aggregate-and-group): Aggregation expressions (count, len, sum, mean, median, min, max, first, last, n_unique), group_by with agg, whole-group aggregates, and rank methods in Tabsdata transformers.
- [Join Tables](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/join-tables): Joins two Tabsdata tables with `join()` on one or more key columns, covering the inner, left, right, full, semi and anti join types, `left_on`/`right_on`, and `suffix` for duplicate names.
- [Concatenate Tables](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/concatenate-tables): Concatenate tables with `concat()` and its `how` modes (vertical, vertical_relaxed, diagonal, diagonal_relaxed), with transformer examples and the None-handling rules.
- [Clean and Sort Data](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/clean-data): Covers handling null and NaN values, sorting rows with sort() and its descending and nulls_last options, and changing column types with cast(), str.to_date/to_datetime/to_time/to_integer, and dt.to_string in Tabsdata transformers.
- [Inspect a TableFrame](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/inspect-a-tableframe): Inspect a TableFrame's schema, dtypes, column checks, emptiness, and query plan with tf.dtypes, has_cols, assert_has_cols, has_same_schema, is_empty, empty, clear, explain, and show_graph.
- [Reshape Data](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/transformations/reshape-data): Covers reshaping Tabsdata tables with transformers: pivoting rows to columns with extract_as_columns(), unpivoting with extract_as_rows(), and expanding structs with unnest().

## Tutorials: Subscribe data to

- [Amazon S3](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/amazon-s3): Writes Tabsdata tables to Amazon S3 as Parquet files using an S3 destination connection and the @subscriber decorator, covering paths, input_tables, and trigger_by.
- [Apache Druid](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/druid): Subscribes Tabsdata tables to Apache Druid with the DruidDest connector, covering DruidDest options, the staging S3 location, if_table_exists, time_column, and segment_granularity.
- [AWS Glue](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/catalogs/aws-glue): Subscriber setup for writing Tabsdata tables to Amazon S3 as Parquet files and registering them in AWS Glue Data Catalog as Iceberg tables, using td.S3Destination and td.AWSGlue.
- [Azure Blob Storage](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/azure): Writes Tabsdata tables to Azure Blob Storage as Parquet files using `@subscriber`, `AzureBlobDest`, and an Azure account key connection definition.
- [BigQuery](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/bigquery): Subscribes Tabsdata tables to BigQuery: the BigQueryDestConn connection spec with GCS staging and service account credentials, the @subscriber decorator with BigQueryDest, if_table_exists, and schema_evolution options.
- [ClickHouse](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/clickhouse): Writes Tabsdata tables out to ClickHouse with the ClickHouseDest subscriber destination, covering table mapping, if_table_exists and schema_evolution options, S3 staging, and the tabsdata[clickhouse] install.
- [Databricks](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/databricks): Writes Tabsdata tables out to Databricks with a subscriber, covering DatabricksDestConn, if_table_exists, schema_evolution, and merging by key.
- [Google Cloud Storage](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/gcp): Writes Tabsdata tables to Google Cloud Storage as Parquet objects using a GCSDest subscriber, with bucket, project, base path, service account credentials, and the paths option.
- [Iceberg on AWS Glue](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/aws-iceberg): Tabsdata subscriber that writes tables to Amazon S3 as Parquet files and registers them in AWS Glue Iceberg tables, with catalog, auto-create, partition and schema strategy options.
- [Local Files](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/local-file-system): Writes Tabsdata tables to local Parquet files using a LocalFileDest subscriber, covering paths, input_tables, connection config, and the trigger_by default.
- [MariaDB](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/mariadb): Shows how to subscribe a Tabsdata collection to write its tables out to MariaDB with the MySQLDest connector, covering if_table_exists options and subscriber code.
- [MongoDB](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/mongodb): Writes Tabsdata input tables to MongoDB collections using a @subscriber with MongoDBDest, covering collections_with_ids, if_collection_exists, update_existing, and the connectionDef YAML.
- [MSSQL](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/mssql): Covers writing Tabsdata tables to SQL Server with a `@subscriber` using `MSSQLDest`, including `tables`, `if_table_exists="replace"`, the `mssql+pyodbc` connection URI, and `collection/table` inputs.
- [MySQL](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/mysql): Writes Tabsdata input tables to MySQL destination tables using the MySQLDest connector, covering the tables list, if_table_exists options, connection setup, and driver requirements.
- [Oracle](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/oracle): Writes Tabsdata input tables to Oracle with the `OracleDest` destination, covering the `oracledb` driver requirement, `if_table_exists` options, and subscriber registration.
- [Postgres](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/postgres): Writes Tabsdata table frames to PostgreSQL with the @subscriber decorator and PostgresDest, covering tables, if_table_exists, the psycopg2-binary driver requirement, and connection setup.
- [Snowflake](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/snowflake): Subscribes Tabsdata tables to Snowflake: the SnowflakeDestConn connection definition, @subscriber with SnowflakeDest and if_table_exists options, and merge into SQL destinations.
- [StarRocks](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/subscribers/starrocks): Writes Tabsdata tables to StarRocks via a subscriber with StarRocksDest, covering connection YAML, staging to S3, if_table_exists, schema_evolution, and the tabsdata[starrocks] install.
- [Unity Catalog](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/catalogs/unity-catalog): Tabsdata subscriber that writes Tabsdata tables to Unity Catalog managed Delta tables in Databricks via DatabricksDestination, covering its host, token, volume, warehouse, and schema options.

## Tutorials: Trigger your functions

- [Manually Trigger a Function](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/trigger-setup/manual): Describes running a Tabsdata function on demand via a manual trigger, including testing scheduled functions and the default for publishers with no trigger configured.
- [Schedule a Cron Trigger](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/trigger-setup/cron): Explains how to schedule a Tabsdata publisher or function with a CronTrigger using crontab masks evaluated in UTC, with a worked example of an hourly publisher.
- [Trigger a Function from a Table Commit](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/trigger-setup/table-commit): Explains the trigger_by parameter for Tabsdata functions, which narrows automatic runs to chosen input tables, names non-input tables, or disables table-commit triggering with an empty list.
- [Trigger off CDC in an SQL Database](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/trigger-setup/cdc): Covers CDC stream sources for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and IBM Db2 (`MySQLCdcStreamSrc`, `PostgresCdcStreamSrc`, `Db2CdcStreamSrc`), their `start_from` options, PostgreSQL replication slots, and batch timing.
- [Trigger off a Kafka Stream](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/trigger-setup/kafka): Tabsdata Kafka stream source guide: setting up a kafka-topic-in connection and a stream publisher with KafkaStreamSrc, batch_* parameters, schema, and dlq_topic for failed messages.

## Tutorials: Manage your resources

- [Create a Project](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-projects/create): Explains how to create a Tabsdata project through an AI agent, covering the name and description fields, the generated project ID, and setting the new project as active.
- [Update a Project](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-projects/update): Explains how to update a Tabsdata project's name and description with an AI agent, noting that the project id and its groups and collections are preserved.
- [Delete a Project](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-projects/delete): Deletes a Tabsdata project through the AI agent, showing the confirmation step and the groups and collections removed with it, and that the name becomes available for reuse.
- [Create a Group](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-groups/create): Creates a Tabsdata group inside a project, covering the group name and description fields, the data product collection type, and how the seeded sources and destinations groups differ.
- [Update a Group](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-groups/update): Renames a Tabsdata group and updates its description, covering the update command, the name and description fields, and the restriction on system groups default, sources, and destinations.
- [Delete a Group](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-groups/delete): Deletes a Tabsdata group and every collection and table it contains, with a confirmation step and notes on how dependent functions are left frozen.
- [Create a Collection](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-collections/create): Shows how to create a Tabsdata collection through an AI agent, covering collection types (data product vs. source/destination), the default group, connection requirements, and the group-connection mismatch error.
- [Update a Collection](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-collections/update): Updates an existing Tabsdata collection's name and description through the agent or CLI, covering rename behavior, the group and type limits, and connection side effects.
- [Delete a Collection](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-collections/delete): Deletes a Tabsdata collection through an AI agent session, showing the dependency check, confirmation step, cascade of functions and tables, and frozen functions in other collections.
- [Register a Function](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-functions/register): Registers a Tabsdata function from a Python file into a collection, covering the transformer and function registration steps, naming, versioning, and the update option.
- [Delete a Function](https://docs.tabsdata.com/tutorials/managing-functions/delete): Explains how to delete a registered function, noting that its output tables remain and downstream functions that read them stop running until re-registered.

## Server administration: Dependency Installation

- [Install Tabsdata](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/install): Installs the tabsdata Python package into a virtual environment on Linux, macOS, or Windows using uv, pip, conda, pyenv, or venv, with Python 3.12.13 or later and an Anthropic or OpenAI API key.
- [Install Third-Party Database Drivers](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/third-party-database-drivers): Explains how to install third-party database drivers (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server ODBC) for Tabsdata connectors using a requirements file with `tdkserver venv update` and the EKS init configs.

## Server administration: Configure Your AI Agent

- [Configure Your AI Agent](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/connect-agent): Install the Tabsdata skill for your coding agents with tdk ai agents install, then log in so each agent acts through your session.

## Server administration: Deploy a Server

- [Deploy on k-minus](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/kminus): Quickstart a local Tabsdata Server or manage its k-minus lifecycle step by step.
- [Deploy on AWS EKS](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/eks-install): Covers installing Tabsdata on AWS EKS: priority classes, kubeconfig access, RDS PostgreSQL and S3 configuration, tdkserver init/assess/create/start, port-forward login, and optional worker log setup.
- [Deploy on Azure AKS](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/aks-install): Installs Tabsdata on Azure AKS using a PostgreSQL flexible server and Blob Storage, covering node pools, priority classes, tdkserver init/assess/create/start, and optional worker logs.
- [Deploy on Google GKE](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/gke-install): Install Tabsdata on Google GKE: required GCP resources, priority classes, node pools, optional Cloud Logging worker logs, Cloud SQL and GCS configuration, tdkserver assess, create and start.
- Deployment: your cloud, hybrid or fully on-premises, on Kubernetes (kminus locally, EKS, AKS, GKE); your data never leaves your network.

## Server administration: Server Management

- [Quickstart a Server](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/quickstart): Quickstart a Tabsdata server with `tdkserver quickstart`, covering the default kminus, eks, aks and gke providers, the `--config`, `--fill` and `--yes` options, and login.
- [Initialize a Server](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/initialize): Covers `tdkserver init`, which writes an editable config folder under ~/.tabsdata/instances/<name> with default settings, using options like --instance and --provider, before creating and starting a server.
- [Create a Server](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/create): Covers `tdkserver create --instance`, which builds a server instance from the init config folder, setting the LLM API key, port assignment with `--port`, and checking with `tdkserver list`.
- [Start a Server](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/start): Describes starting a Tabsdata server instance with the `tdkserver start` command, including the `--instance` option, after an instance has been built by `tdkserver create`.
- [Stop a Server](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/stop): Explains how to stop a running Tabsdata server with `tdkserver stop` while keeping its registration, configuration, tables and functions, plus checking runs with `tdk fnrun list` and restarting after config changes.
- [Delete a Server](https://docs.tabsdata.com/server-admin/delete): Deletes a local kminus server instance with `tdkserver trash`, covering the stop and confirmation steps, the irreversible data loss, and the EKS exception.

## Reference

- [CLI reference](https://docs.tabsdata.com/cli/): [tdk](https://docs.tabsdata.com/cli/tdk) for functions, tables, plans and logs; [tdkserver](https://docs.tabsdata.com/cli/tdkserver) for servers; [interactive CLI](https://docs.tabsdata.com/cli/explorer).
- [API reference](https://docs.tabsdata.com/api/)
- [Release notes](https://docs.tabsdata.com/release-notes): 2.2.1 fixed Kafka schema-registry sources, merge initial load and truncate on Databricks, Snowflake and BigQuery, and a stream publisher data-loss case; 2.2.0 added CDC full load for Postgres, MySQL and Db2, data quality trends, service tokens and `tdkserver quickstart --config` and `--fill`.
